name: Ubud
tagline: Rice terraces, temples and slow mornings
summary: Ubud is a useful inland Bali base for culture and landscapes. Group nearby town stops and use a separate driver day for rice terraces and water temples to reduce traffic backtracking.
seasonNote: Dry-season shoulder months are often pleasant; July–August is busy and rain is more frequent around November–March. Nyepi affects island movement.
arrival: Arrive at Denpasar airport and allow a long road transfer; traffic can make the journey much slower than the map suggests.
gettingAround: Walk the compact centre where practical; hire a driver for rural clusters. Scooter riding needs suitable skill, licence and insurance.
cashTip: Carry rupiah for small entries and warungs; larger venues usually accept cards.
foodTip: Try nasi campur and fresh cooked dishes; pork and shrimp paste are common in Balinese food.
buyTip: Look for textiles, baskets and woodwork; ask how pieces were made and check export/import restrictions.
baseArea: Central Ubud for walking or a nearby quieter lane.

connections.note: Road transfer to Denpasar plus flight; traffic and airport formalities extra.
Approximate road-and-flight planning allowance, not a schedule.

reviewSummary: Visitor snapshots identify the Monkey Forest and Campuhan among established favourites. The Monkey Forest score retrieved was 4.2/5 from 35,722 reviews; close wildlife encounters require following the sanctuary rules.
